fields.scientific_name: Cessation of ACh-driven signalling, repolarization, SR Ca2+ reuptake and reshielding of actin-binding sites

temporal_scope.start_condition: Motor neuron stops releasing ACh (normal pathway); alternatively ATP depletion/fatigue can terminate contraction without normal relaxation
temporal_scope.end_condition: Actin-binding sites reshielded and fibre loses tension (normal pathway)

exceptions.description: A muscle also can stop contracting when it runs out of ATP and becomes fatigued; this ATP-depletion route is not modelled here as normal relaxation and does not produce the ST_FIBRE_RELAXED effect.
exceptions.evidence_quote: A muscle also can stop contracting when it runs out of ATP and becomes fatigued ( Figure 10.9 ).

support.quote: Muscle contraction usually stops when signaling from the motor neuron ends, which repolarizes the sarcolemma and T-tubules, and closes the voltage-gated calcium channels in the SR.

ATP-driven pumps will move Ca ++ out of the sarcoplasm back into the SR. This results in the “reshielding” of the actin-binding sites on the thin filaments. Without the ability to form cross-bridges between the thin and thick filaments, the muscle fiber loses its tension and relaxes.

fields.definition: Ca2+ released into the sarcoplasm binds troponin, causing tropomyosin to slide away and expose myosin-binding sites on actin

support.quote: The first step in the process of contraction is for Ca ++ to bind to troponin so that tropomyosin can slide away from the binding sites on the actin strands.

As long as Ca ++ ions remain in the sarcoplasm to bind to troponin, which keeps the actin-binding sites “unshielded,” and as long as ATP is available to drive the cross-bridge cycling and the pulling of actin strands by myosin, the muscle fiber will continue to shorten to an anatomical limit.

The local membrane of the fiber will depolarize as positively charged sodium ions (Na + ) enter, triggering an action potential that spreads to the rest of the membrane which will depolarize, including the T-tubules.
This triggers the release of calcium ions (Ca ++ ) from storage in the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR).
Tropomyosin is a protein that winds around the chains of the actin filament and covers the myosin-binding sites to prevent actin from binding to myosin.
The first step in the process of contraction is for Ca ++ to bind to troponin so that tropomyosin can slide away from the binding sites on the actin strands.

As long as Ca ++ ions remain in the sarcoplasm to bind to troponin, which keeps the actin-binding sites “unshielded,” and as long as ATP is available to drive the cross-bridge cycling and the pulling of actin strands by myosin, the muscle fiber will continue to shorten to an anatomical limit.
The contraction of a striated muscle fiber occurs as the sarcomeres, linearly arranged within myofibrils, shorten as myosin heads pull on the actin filaments.
Muscle contraction usually stops when signaling from the motor neuron ends, which repolarizes the sarcolemma and T-tubules, and closes the voltage-gated calcium channels in the SR.
ATP-driven pumps will move Ca ++ out of the sarcoplasm back into the SR.
Without the ability to form cross-bridges between the thin and thick filaments, the muscle fiber loses its tension and relaxes.

issue_resolution.reason: Clarified that the neural-off route is the modelled normal relaxation pathway; ATP-depletion/fatigue remains an explicit exception and is not conflated with normal relaxation. The process no longer asserts the neuronal-off route as the sole possible termination.

No process/relation fields were updated for this issue because the mislocated state subject (ENT_SR vs sarcoplasm) cannot be corrected within the allowed process/relation field set; ST_CA_IN_SARCOPLASM remains with subject_ref ENT_SR as an SR Ca2+-location change. The issue is noted but not resolved by this patch.

Relation source changed to ENT_TROPONIN_TROPOMYOSIN and target to ENT_ACTIN_MYOSIN_SARCOMERE, so the source now matches the actor binding Ca2+ and the target is the actin site whose exposure changes, consistent with the quote.

Observable role mapping changed to contractile_filaments for both source and target of REL_CROSSBRIDGE_ACTIN_MYOSIN, aligning the observable with the relation semantics (myosin-head binding to actin within the actin-myosin system) rather than using the regulatory complex as the source actor.

No entity/process fields were updated for this issue; state subject mapping was corrected in state_upgrade (ST_ACTIN_SITES_SHIELDED and ST_ACTIN_SITES_UNSHIELDED now have subject_ref ENT_ACTIN_MYOSIN_SARCOMERE), but this repair iteration's operations do not include entity fields. The issue is noted for verification.
